Set $y = (x - 3)^2 - 2$ and solve for $x$ on the domain $x > 4$ (where $x - 3 > 1 > 0$):
$$(x - 3)^2 = y + 2 \implies x - 3 = \sqrt{y + 2} \implies x = 3 + \sqrt{y + 2}$$
$$g^{-1}(x) = 3 + \sqrt{x + 2}$$

Determine the domain of $g^{-1}$ from the range of $g$ on $x > 4$:
$$x > 4 \implies x - 3 > 1 \implies (x - 3)^2 > 1 \implies (x - 3)^2 - 2 > -1$$
$$\text{Domain of } g^{-1}: \quad x > -1 \quad (\text{or } (-1, \infty))$$
